tara: Quick heads-up — onboarding concordia-7b-hybrid (int4) is showing a reproducible quality drift vs our reference runs. Ran the standard eval suite (qa/summarize/chat) and F1/ROUGE dipped ~5-8% on a small prompt set.

ivan: Can you paste a minimal repro and which tokenizer/token ids you used? Is this HF tokenizer or a model-specific one? :thinking:

tara: Using the model repo tokenizer (concordia/tokenizer.json) + our usual normalizer. Minimal repro below — same prompt, same seed, different outputs between float32 baseline and int4 quantized.

sam: Two quick things that have bitten us before: 1) rotary frequency scaling mismatch (headwise vs shared scale) causes subtle ordering diffs, 2) token id offsets from tokenizer conversions break KV cache indexing and you get drift as context grows.

morgan: I ran a small ablation. Command I used: `./scripts/onboard_eval.sh --model concordia-7b --quant int4-channelwise --seed 42 --batch 4 --prompts tests/concordia_smoke.json`

tara: Paste of the output diff (truncated):
```
BASELINE: ...the procedure requires logging the user's consent before proceeding.
INT4: .....procedure requires logging the userconsent before proceeding.
DIFF: tokenization gap around "user consent" -> produced as single token in int4 run
```

ivan: That looks like a tokenizer merge. Could you run `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('concordia/tokenizer.json').encode('user consent').ids)"` and compare to our canonical tokenizer? Also paste the first 16 token ids for the prompt in both runs.

tara: Ran that — concordia tokenizer encodes `user consent` as [4521] (single token). Our canonical tokenizer encodes as [452, 1, 78, 21]. So it's definitely a vocab mapping difference.

sam: If the tokenizer maps a multiword into one id, and our conversion tool remapped ids incorrectly (or left old merges), the KV cache alignment will go off-by-N after that token and outputs wander. Not necessarily a rotary bug yet.

lee: I ran a quick quant sweep: int4-channelwise vs int4-symmetric vs int8. Channelwise int4 preserved logits patterns best, symmetric int4 had slightly higher perplexity. But all quant formats show the tokenizer-induced regression in the QA test where the merged token occurs. Numbers: PPL baseline=18.4, int4-channel=19.6, int4-symm=21.1, int8=18.7.

ci-bot: CI: onboard/quality/concordia-7b-int4 — failed (F1 drop > 5%) — logs: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/823/logs

morgan: Another inexpensive check: run the tokenizer round-trip on a 10k sample and assert id-level equality after our conversion script (tools/convert_vocab.py). Also try running the model with `rotary_scale=0.5` vs `1.0` — if the outputs diverge more with one setting it's a hint.

tara: Agreed. Next steps: 1) run tokenizer roundtrip audit and fix convert_vocab mapping if needed, 2) run rotary-scale ablation and kvcache index trace to ensure no off-by-one, 3) re-run quant sweep after tokenizer fix. I'll open a triage ticket and assign to @ivan (tokenizer) and @sam (runtime/rotary/kv).

ivan: I'll take the tokenizer audit now. If mapping is wrong I'll regenerate a patched tokenizer and push a deterministic test to the onboarding harness.

sam: I'll add a small kvcache index tracer in the runtime that prints token ids -> kv indices for the first 128 tokens so we can catch misalignment early.

tara: Thanks — please drop links to PRs in this thread. If we fix tokenizer mapping and the regression persists we'll escalate to a deeper rotary/quant investigation. :thumbsup:
